people.name: Yoshinori Ohsumi
people.key_contribution: Discovered autophagy genes in yeast (ATG genes) and elucidated mechanism; translated to mammalian systems; basis of all fasting-autophagy science
notable_works: Tsukada & Ohsumi 1993 FEBS Lett — vacuolar morphology mutants

people.name: Mark Mattson, PhD
people.affiliation: National Institute on Aging (NIH) / Johns Hopkins
people.key_contribution: NEJM 2019 landmark review on IF effects on health, aging, disease; IF-BDNF-neuroprotection research
notable_works: Mattson MP et al. NEJM 2019 — Effects of IF on Health, Aging, and Disease
Multiple studies on fasting and neuroplasticity

people.name: Valter Longo, PhD
people.affiliation: USC Leonard Davis School of Gerontology
people.key_contribution: Developed FMD protocol; research on fasting and stem cell regeneration (Cell Stem Cell 2014); IF + cancer chemotherapy interaction
notable_works: Longo VD & Panda S Cell Metabolism 2016 — Fasting, Circadian Rhythms
Cheng CW...Longo VD Cell Stem Cell 2014 — Prolonged Fasting and Stem Cells

people.name: Satchin Panda, PhD
people.key_contribution: Established TRE in mice + humans; myCircadianClock app; circadian clock gene research; 10h TRE in metabolic syndrome patients (Wilkinson 2020)
notable_works: Hatori M...Panda S Cell Metabolism 2012 — TRE in mice
Wilkinson MJ...Panda S Cell Metabolism 2020 — 10h TRE in metabolic syndrome

people.name: Jason Fung, MD
people.key_contribution: Popularized IF for T2D management and obesity; 'The Obesity Code', 'The Complete Guide to Fasting'; controversial in some claims but raised mainstream awareness

people.name: Michelle Harvie, PhD
people.key_contribution: First RCT of 5:2 IF vs daily caloric restriction (2011); showed equivalent weight loss and metabolic benefits with better adherence in 5:2 arm
notable_works: Harvie MN et al. Int J Obesity 2011 — 5:2 RCT

people.name: Frank Madeo, PhD
people.key_contribution: Identified spermidine as autophagy inducer and longevity mimetic; showed dietary spermidine associated with longevity in population studies
notable_works: Madeo F et al. Science 2018 — Spermidine: a physiological autophagy inducer acting as an anti-aging vitamin in humans

people.name: Eric Ravussin, PhD
people.role: Metabolic Physiologist — CR and IF Research
people.affiliation: Pennington Biomedical Research Center / CALERIE trial
people.key_contribution: CALERIE trial (Caloric Restriction and Its Effects): 2-year CR RCT demonstrating metabolic benefits; comparative CR vs IF metabolism research
notable_works: Ravussin E et al. JAMA Intern Med 2015 — 2-year CR pilot

molecules.name: Beta-Hydroxybutyrate (BHB)
molecules.role_in_domain: Primary ketone fuel for brain/muscle during fasting; HDAC inhibitor with epigenetic effects; suppresses ghrelin

molecules.name: mTORC1 (mechanistic Target of Rapamycin Complex 1)
molecules.role_in_domain: Master switch: active = anabolism/cell growth; inhibited by fasting/rapamycin = autophagy on; sensor of amino acids, growth factors

molecules.name: AMPK (AMP-activated Protein Kinase)
molecules.role_in_domain: Activated by low ATP/fasting → activates fat oxidation, mitochondrial biogenesis, autophagy; inhibits mTOR

molecules.name: LC3-II (Microtubule-associated Protein 1A/1B Light Chain 3B)
molecules.role_in_domain: Lipidated form (LC3-II) decorates autophagosome membrane; biomarker of autophagy activation in research

molecules.name: Spermidine
molecules.role_in_domain: Natural polyamine in food (wheat germ, soybeans); induces autophagy via EP300 inhibition; declines with age

molecules.name: IGF-1 (Insulin-like Growth Factor 1)
molecules.role_in_domain: Reduced by fasting → releases pituitary from GH inhibition → GH pulses increase → protein sparing; drives mTOR in fed state

molecules.name: SIRT1 (Sirtuin 1)
molecules.role_in_domain: Activated by NAD+ (rises with fasting/exercise/NMN) → deacetylates PGC-1α → mitochondrial biogenesis; deacetylates p53 → DNA repair

molecules.name: FoxO3A (Forkhead Box O3)
molecules.role_in_domain: Activated when IGF-1/insulin low (fasting) → activates stress resistance and stem cell self-renewal genes; associated with longevity in multiple human studies

organizations.name: National Institute on Aging (NIA)
organizations.role: Primary funder of US IF and longevity research including Mattson's lab work

organizations.name: Salk Institute for Biological Studies
organizations.role: Panda lab TRE/circadian research center; source of myCircadianClock app research

organizations.name: USC Longevity Institute (Longo Lab)
organizations.role: FMD protocol development; fasting + cancer therapy research; clinical trials

organizations.name: CALERIE Trial Consortium
organizations.role: Multi-site 2-year CR trial; highest quality long-term RCT of caloric restriction in non-obese humans

case_studies.title: Sutton 2018 — Early TRE Improves Insulin Sensitivity without Weight Loss
case_studies.description: 5-week RCT, overweight men; eating window 6h (8AM-2PM) vs 12h control; significant improvement in insulin sensitivity, blood pressure, oxidative stress — WITHOUT caloric restriction or weight loss; landmark for metabolic circadian alignment

case_studies.title: Wilkinson 2020 — 10h TRE in Metabolic Syndrome
case_studies.description: 12-week 10h TRE in metabolic syndrome patients (most on statin/antihypertensive); significant reductions in weight, BMI, visceral fat, blood pressure, LDL, HbA1c; no change in medication required; real-world clinical evidence for TRE

case_studies.title: Longo 2014 — Prolonged Fasting and Stem Cell Regeneration (Mouse)
case_studies.description: Mice subjected to 2-4 day fasting cycles showed 40% increase in hematopoietic stem cell regeneration after chemotherapy; PKA/IGF-1 pathway mechanism; basis for FMD protocol in cancer support context
